source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. The Mughals — Origins and Rulers
points: The Mughals were descended from **Timur** (father's side) and **Genghis Khan/Chinggis Khan** (mother's side) — though they disliked the term 'Mughal' (Mongol).

sub: **Babur (1526–1530)** — won the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)** against Ibrahim Lodi; founded the empire.
**Humayun (1530–40, 1555–56)** — lost to **Sher Shah Suri**, regained the throne.

sections.heading: 2. Relations with Other Rulers
points: The Mughals campaigned against, and allied with, many rulers — especially the **Rajputs**.
**Marriage alliances** (e.g. with **Amber/Jaipur** and **Jodhpur**) tied Rajputs to the empire; many became high **mansabdars**.
But **Mewar (Sisodiya Rajputs)** and later the **Marathas, Sikhs, Jats and Ahoms** resisted Mughal expansion.

sections.heading: 3. Mansabdari and Jagirs
points: **Mansabdars** = officials given a **rank (mansab)**; introduced by **Akbar**.
**Zat** = personal rank/status and pay; **Sawar** = number of **horsemen** a mansabdar had to maintain.
In place of cash salary, many were assigned **jagirs** (revenue assignments) — but they usually **did not live there**; officials collected the revenue.
Nobles came from diverse backgrounds — **Turani, Irani, Rajput, Indian Muslim, Deccani**.

sections.heading: 4. Akbar's Policies
points: **Sulh-i-kul** = 'universal peace/tolerance' — a policy of **religious harmony** and impartiality between faiths.
Abolished the **jizya** (tax on non-Muslims) and the pilgrimage tax.
**Din-i-Ilahi** — a small circle of followers around a set of ethical ideals.
**Todar Mal** designed the **zabt** land-revenue system (revenue fixed as a cash amount per crop, based on surveys).
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama** (incl. the **Ain-i-Akbari**), a detailed account of the empire.

sections.heading: 5. Later Mughals and Decline
points: The empire reached its greatest extent under **Aurangzeb**, but his long **Deccan campaigns** and the **re-imposition of jizya** strained it.
After 1707 the empire **weakened**; provincial governors and new powers (**Marathas, Sikhs, Nawabs**) grew independent.
**Zamindars** and peasants sometimes rebelled against Mughal authority.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Babur → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb.
First Battle of Panipat (1526): Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi; Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun.
Mansabdar rank: zat (status/pay) + sawar (horsemen); jagir = revenue assignment.
Akbar: sulh-i-kul, abolished jizya, Din-i-Ilahi; Todar Mal = zabt; Abul Fazl = Akbarnama/Ain-i-Akbari.
Aurangzeb re-imposed jizya; empire declined after 1707.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Zat** = rank/status & pay; **sawar** = number of horsemen — don't swap.
**Sulh-i-kul** (Akbar) = tolerance; **Aurangzeb** re-imposed the **jizya**.
**Ain-i-Akbari / Akbarnama** was written by **Abul Fazl**.
The **zabt** revenue system is linked to **Todar Mal** under **Akbar**.
